title: Systemic Hemodynamic–Immune–Endothelial–Liver Dynamics in Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome: Discovery of Immune Resilience Signatures
summary: Children and adults born with a heart that has only one functioning pumping chamber (a univentricular heart, e.g. hypoplastic left heart syndrome) undergo staged surgery (Fontan palliation). The resulting special circulation strains the blood vessels, liver, lymphatic system and immune system over the years. This observational study examines how well the immune system copes with this long-term strain ('immune resilience'). We compare 56 affected people with 56 people who have a different, biventricular heart defect that was also successfully corrected. It is purely observational: no treatment and no additional procedures. Only a small, age-adapted amount of blood is taken within routine blood draws, and existing ultrasound and MRI images are re-analysed. Using modern methods we measure special vessel-wall cells, immune cells and protein patterns in the blood, to find early warning signs of organ strain and patterns that mark a particularly resilient immune system. Participants are assessed over two years at three timepoints (baseline, 12 and 24 months). The results should help tailor follow-up care and quality of life in the future.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age 5–50 years; confirmed univentricular or control diagnosis (d-TGA/ToF) by echocardiography ± cardiac MRI; ≥12 months after Fontan palliation or arterial switch / ToF correction; hemodynamically stable; written informed consent (for minors: both legal guardians or the sole-custody holder, plus the minor's assent).
Exclusion criteria:
Active infection/sepsis within 4 weeks; severe renal insufficiency (eGFR below 20 ml/min/1.73 m²); active malignancy/hematologic neoplasia; systemic autoimmune disease under immunosuppression; known HIV or HCV infection; prior organ or bone-marrow transplantation; pregnancy; lack of capacity to consent.
